entries.rationale: The target expression combines A-B with A∩C, so the decisive content is the exact three-set region mask inside A. A U-bounded three-set Venn can show which A/B/C membership cells are retained and why the equivalent form is A-(B-C); this is question-specific and materially clarifies the set identity.

entries.role: graph-defined intersection avoidance and slope-range explanation
entries.rationale: A is defined as a graph and B as the origin-centered line y=mx; A∩B=∅ is therefore a graph-intersection condition over a line family. A question-specific graph of the branches, excluded point/asymptotic behavior, and admissible versus intersecting slopes is the direct visual witness for the requested range of m.

entries.role: no visual role; finite-set membership check is clearer textually
entries.rationale: The task is to match the two parameterized elements of A against the three explicit expressions in B and enforce strictness. A generic inclusion Venn would not encode the parameter-dependent element identities or the case check, so it would duplicate rather than clarify the algebraic membership reasoning; the source is clear without a visual.

The two compound terms reduce to B and B^c, whose union is U. A U-bounded two-set Venn can make the complement coverage transparent, but the same result follows cleanly from distributive and complement laws, so the visual has pedagogical value without being indispensable.

The maximum and minimum of |A∩B| are determined by the feasible overlap and outside regions under |U|=50, |A|=25, and |B|=32. A labeled cardinality Venn, ideally with separate maximum and minimum configurations, directly exposes the extreme arrangements and the lower-bound total-cardinality constraint.
